result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B wins on substance. It gives purpose-based names for both colors and spacing, a test a new token must pass (it must be clearly different from its neighbours, otherwise it merges into an existing one), and a named owner who signs off, all in a friendly tone. A is shorter and clear, but 'Stop adding...' and 'will be bounced in review' read as scolding, and its example `space-400` is a scale step that doesn't say what the value is for. Both answers wrap the message in commentary before and after it, so both lose points on paste-readiness. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A does better on the substance. Its spacing names describe use as well as role. It gives a clear test for additions (a new value must be clearly different from its neighbors, otherwise it merges into an existing one), and it has a named owner who signs off. B's naming pattern is solid, but `space-400` is a scale step rather than a purpose, it doesn't say how to decide whether an addition belongs, and lines like "Stop adding..." and "will be bounced" read as scolding. Both put preamble and closing notes around the Slack text, so neither is fully paste-ready, though both messages stay under 120 words.
